answer: Each epoch the beacon pays one walnut for judged output, but an identity's share scales with the square of the tenure the mesa tallies for it. Only epochs bearing judged output enter that tally; a hollow epoch builds none. Split one operator's work across $k$ clones and the tenure splits too: $k$ identities of tenure $t$ draw $kt^2$ of walnut where one identity of tenure $kt$ draws $(kt)^2$. The bill is that convex premium, paid in walnut every epoch, plus each clone re-earning its own attested epochs from nothing — tenure transfers to no sibling. A newcomer tallies from zero at the mesa.
